purpose: Two six-frame whole-miner reeling atlases. Each pose includes the miner, connected arms, handle, winch and short rope as one authored sprite. Rope endpoint is the pivot; feet and axle are independent registration checks. No runtime assembly of disconnected arm components.
source_provenance: Built-in image_gen originals copied byte-for-byte. No recoloring, raster crop, scaling, alpha edits or compositing was applied by code. Unity sprite rectangles select poses without changing the source PNG. Generated source paths and complete prompts are retained below.

coordinate_contract.source_rectangles: Whole-source pixels, top-left origin; arbitrary non-overlapping per-frame rectangles are supported.
coordinate_contract.anchors: All anchors use whole-source top-left pixels. Rope endpoint is measured from each visible short rope/alpha silhouette. Foot and axle are supplied registration reference points, not per-frame pixel detections.
coordinate_contract.unity_rectangles: Same original source pixels, converted to bottom-left origin before platform texture downscaling.
coordinate_contract.pivot: Normalized to each individual frame, bottom-left origin, exactly at the rope endpoint. Foot is not the pivot.
coordinate_contract.registration: The import contract checks that supplied foot/axle reference offsets relative to the measured rope endpoint vary by at most 2 source pixels. This validates metadata consistency, not mechanical consistency of the image pixels.
coordinate_contract.alpha_top: Use the fixed local source y=18 for runtime sizing. Measured tops below use alpha>200 to ignore the 1-pixel antialias fringe; actual artwork is unchanged.

assets.title: P1橙色矿工与绞盘整体六帧收线动画
generation_prompts:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: production Unity 2D SIX FRAME looping sprite sheet. Create a coherent hand drawn animation sheet of the orange gold miner REELING a wooden rope winch. References: first image is the exact friendly orange uniform, yellow hard hat, white beard miner identity; second image is winch material/style. Transparent background.
Output one landscape 3 columns by 2 rows grid, 1536x1024 pixels, six equal 512x512 cells in row-major order. No labels or grid lines. Every cell is the SAME fixed camera full assembly: entire miner on left, smaller wooden rope winch on right, both boots, full arms naturally attached to orange shoulders, brown gloved right hand holding the crank. Whole silhouette fits each cell x=60..460, y=60..450; hat top y=60, boot sole y=445. Miner is about 310px tall, machine about 135px tall, a squat broad cylindrical drum with beige twisted hemp rope and fixed wooden supports. Feet planted. Fixed axle x=300,y=340. A small fixed rope outlet on front bottom of the machine at x=380,y=425; short beige rope ends at x=380,y=450. No long rope, hook, ground or shadows outside assembly.
Six distinct phases of ONE FULL crank revolution: 0,60,120,180,240,300 degrees. Crank grip travels in a SMALL ellipse around the actual drum axle, not around the machine. Shoulder and elbow naturally bend to keep hand tightly grasping it, no disconnected limbs. The free left hand braces upper machine frame consistently. This is an animation sheet, not six separate composition sketches. Across all six cells lock hat/head/body position and scale, boots, machine base and drum/axle and rope outlet exactly. Only arms, hands, crank grip and subtle rope winding highlights vary. No machine rocking, no entire machine rotation, no duplicated handles, no tools/pickaxe, no floating hands, no face morphing, no text. Match warm polished cartoon shading and dark brown outlines in references. Clear silhouettes at phone display size.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this six-cell 3×2 transparent sprite sheet into a mechanically consistent single-hand cranking loop. Preserve EXACT same cell grid 1536×1024, miner identity/colors, fixed boots/head/body and wooden machine location. Remove ALL surrounding glow or shadow outside silhouettes, use fully clear transparent gaps.
Most important correction: each frame must have ONLY ONE crank, attached at the LEFT END of the horizontal drum axle, at local cell (240,320). The crank endpoint travels a small vertical ellipse with radii x=45 y=40 around that axle. Near/right arm (viewer left arm rooted at cell (130,225)) turns this single crank. Its gloved hand positions, relative to its cell, are frame0 (195,320), frame1 (218,285), frame2 (263,285), frame3 (285,320), frame4 (263,355), frame5 (218,355). Keep hand physically attached along orange sleeve and elbow. The other/far hand ALWAYS stays in the SAME resting place on the top of the rear wooden frame (320,270) across every frame; never raise it. No disconnected sleeve, no third hand.
Delete all protruding unused cranks at right end and any vertical extra crank in first row. The machine right end has only a short round axle cap. Keep wooden base shape, posts, beige hemp coil and rope outlet IDENTICAL each cell. Reel axle does not move. Only near arm and single crank articulate. Feet and head stay exactly registered. Rope eye at local (338,448), short rope end at (338,480) same in all cells. Do not add text, cell lines, ground, long rope, hook or labels. The result will be cycled as an animation, so invariant geometry is essential.
